3

reveal.html creates presentations with reveal.js, the HTML presentation framework (also used by Jupyter's slide export). Presentations are saved as one HTML file that plays in any browser – offline, without installing anything – and can be edited again.

Slides

The list on the left shows the slides. reveal.js arranges them in two dimensions: main slides from left to right, and sub-slides below a main slide (indented in the list, numbered 2.1, 2.2, …).

Button Function
+ Slide inserts a slide after the current one: title, title and list, section, image, code, quote, blank, Markdown or HTML
+ Sub-slide inserts a sub-slide below the current slide
↑ ↓ move the slide (within its level)
⇥ ⇤ make a main slide a sub-slide of the previous slide, or a sub-slide a main slide
⧉ 🗑 duplicate or delete the slide

With a mouse, slides can also be dragged in the list: dropping on a slide puts the dragged slide before it (at the same level); dropping on the right half of a main slide makes it that slide's last sub-slide. A main slide takes its sub-slides along.

Editing a slide

The middle shows the slide as reveal.js displays it. Click an element to select it, double-click a text (or press Enter) to edit it right there; the bar above offers bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code, link, colour and removing formatting. Esc or Done ends editing.

+ Element adds a heading, text, list, image, code, quote, table, diagram or HTML block after the selected element. The Element tab of the inspector on the right edits the selected element. (The diagram block draws a Mermaid flowchart from text; 📐 Diagram (draw.io) instead adds an image that you draw in the diagram editor: every Save there updates the picture, 📐 Edit diagram in the inspector opens it again, and 📐 Draw a diagram turns any image block into one. The diagram travels inside the picture – a PNG with the draw.io file – also in saved presentations.)

  • heading level and “fit text to the slide”, numbered lists, images (file, alternative text, width, fill the remaining height), code (language with syntax highlighting, line numbers and highlighted steps such as 1|2-3|5), table rows and columns, HTML;
  • appearance (fragment): the element appears on click with an effect (fade in, fade up, grow, shrink, highlight, …); lists can show their points one by one; the order decides which comes first;
  • auto-animate ID: elements with the same ID on consecutive auto-animate slides move smoothly from one to the other;
  • alignment, size and colour; move, duplicate and delete.

A slide can also be written in Markdown or HTML (Slide tab, Content); Markdown supports the reveal.js notation, for example <!-- .element: class="fragment" -->.

Diagrams

A diagram block draws a Mermaid flowchart, typed in the inspector, for example flowchart LR and lines like A[Idea] --> B{Good?} and B -->|yes| C([Slides]). Boxes, rounded boxes, decisions, terminals, databases, hexagons and circles are laid out automatically, like Mermaid import in the diagram editor; other Mermaid diagram types show an error. The drawing is stored in the presentation as SVG, so it needs no Mermaid library and works offline; it takes the text colour of the theme. Saving as PowerPoint leaves diagrams out.

Formulas

Mathematical formulas are written in TeX (LaTeX notation) in any text, Markdown or HTML: $$ … $$ or \[ … \] for a formula on its own line, \( … \) inside a sentence, for example $$\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = \tfrac13$$ or Pythagoras: \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). A single $ stays an ordinary dollar sign. The formulas are typeset with KaTeX in the preview and in the saved presentation, also offline; only presentations that contain formulas include KaTeX (about 0.6 MB). When you edit a text with a formula, you edit its TeX source.

Slide and presentation settings

  • Slide tab: background (colour, CSS gradient, image with size and opacity), transition and speed, auto-animate, visibility (hidden or not counted), vertical position, automatic advance, speaker notes, CSS class.
  • Presentation tab: title, theme (14 reveal.js themes), code colours, transitions, slide size (e.g. 16:9), arrow controls, progress bar, slide numbers, vertical centring, loop, slide number in the address, navigation mode, scrolling page view, automatic advance, language and custom CSS.

Presenting

▶ Present (F5) shows the presentation from the current slide in full screen. Keys: arrows or Space to move, O or Esc overview, S speaker view with notes and timer, F full screen. ↗ presents in a new window (useful with a second screen), 🖨 opens the print view to save a PDF (choose “Save as PDF” in the print dialog) – with Print / PDF with speaker notes each slide is followed by a page with its notes.

Files

Format Open Save
reveal.js presentation (.html) yes – own files completely, other reveal.js presentations with their slides as HTML yes (Save, Ctrl+S)
Markdown (.md) yes – --- separates slides, -- sub-slides, Note: starts speaker notes Save as → Markdown (texts only)
Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) yes – the slide types of the cells (slide, sub-slide, fragment, skip, notes) like jupyter nbconvert --to slides –
PowerPoint (.pptx) yes – converted into blocks: titles, texts with formatting, lists, pictures, tables, notes, backgrounds, transitions, entrance animations as fragments Save as → PowerPoint (blocks laid out top to bottom)

Markdown files and notebooks are converted; saving creates a new HTML presentation. In the Python notebook, Slideshow shows a slide type for each cell and 🎞️ Slides opens the notebook here. Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y) cover all changes.

Scripts in presentations

Slides may contain HTML, and HTML can contain scripts (<script>, event handlers such as onclick, javascript: links). To protect your data, scripts in slides are blocked: the preview, presenting, printing and the saved file show the slides without running them (a Content Security Policy lets only the editor's own scripts – reveal.js, its plugins, formulas – run). When you open a presentation that contains such content, you are asked whether to allow it:

  • Keep blocked (recommended for files from others): the slides are shown, the scripts do not run.
  • Allow scripts (unprotected): only for files you trust. The scripts then run with the rights of this app and could read or change your data in the suite (settings, saved connections, opened files) or send it elsewhere.

The button 🛡 Scripts blocked / ⚠ Scripts allowed in the toolbar shows the state and switches it (allowing asks again). The decision is not stored in the file: a presentation opened again is blocked until you allow it. A presentation saved while its scripts are blocked keeps them, but they stay blocked when the file is opened in a browser.

On phones and tablets

The preview uses the full width; ‹ and › change the slide, Slides opens the slide list and Panels the inspector. Double-tap a text to edit it.
